assessment: This work presents a valuable approach based on a complex systems theoretical framework to characterize diet-host-microbe interactions and develop targeted bacteriotherapies through a three-phase workflow. Despite the partial support of the description and experimental setup of the 'complex systems theoretical approach,' the collected data are solid and advance our understanding of oxalate bacterial metabolism in microbial communities. This study will interest researchers working on gut microbiomes and the possible modulation of host-microbial interactions.
